title: Kubernetes: desired state, pods, and controllers
outcome: Explain how a Deployment leads to running pods and what happens when one disappears.

drawbacks: Workload correctness and platform operations remain.

trace.title: Deployment desired state
trace.detail: Docker packages/runs containers. Kubernetes coordinates desired workloads through an API and controllers. It can use compatible container runtimes; Docker Engine is not a required node runtime for every cluster.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Submit desired state → controller creates/adjusts ReplicaSet → scheduler chooses capacity → kubelet/runtime starts containers → readiness decides traffic eligibility. Remove one lab pod and observe reconciliation, not manual resurrection of the same identity.

Inspect events when a pod is Pending or repeatedly restarting. Image pull, scheduling, process failure, and readiness failure are different states.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A pod is disposable identity, not your only copy of data. Increasing replicas does not make a database transaction safe or a queue effect unique.
